reason: Start with the after-meal situation: the picture says higher glucose prompts pancreatic cells to release insulin.
expectation: I expect insulin to be released into the blood, though I'm not sure how the next muscle step will appear.

alternatives.reason: The lower-glucose message also matters, but I want to follow the after-meal sequence first.

effect: Insulin enters the blood and heads toward muscle, so I can follow the after-meal sequence.
reaction: The route to muscle makes the next step clear.
reason: The muscle picture shows receptors for insulin and glucose nearby, matching the goal of storing glucose.
expectation: I expect the muscle to take in glucose and store some as carbohydrate.

alternatives.reason: I could start the lower-glucose sequence, but I want to finish following insulin first.

effect: The muscle stored glucose as linked chains while insulin stayed outside; the after-meal goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction between the message and the stored material is clear.
reason: The only offered combination starts the lower-glucose sequence for the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release the other hormone into the blood; I don't yet know its name.

effect: The lower-glucose signal produces a blood-carried message that tells the liver to break down its store.
reaction: The contrast with insulin's after-meal message makes the two situations clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it follows the message to the liver's stored carbohydrate.
expectation: I expect the liver to break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver store became smaller as glucose entered the blood, completing the between-meals sequence. The release signal also eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the stored carbohydrate become available as glucose again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to the muscle was worthwhile because it showed glucose becoming a store while insulin remained a message outside the cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the second hormone felt somewhat repetitive after releasing insulin, although it set up the contrast between the two situations.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the hormone to remain outside the muscle cells while glucose became the stored material.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: the pictures and goals explained both sequences, though the last two combinations were the only offered actions.

continue.text: I would try another chapter: comparing the two messages and seeing where the glucose goes made this one understandable, even if some steps were predictable.
